evidence: IT business analysts/architects/systems designers: the #3 top-demand occupation nationally (+34,000 by 2030), needed in 6 of 10 priority sectors.
Programmers and software development professionals: the #2 top-demand occupation nationally (+87,000 by 2030), needed in 7 of 10 sectors.
Industrial Strategy: partnership to train 7.5 million UK workers in essential AI skills by 2030; ESS: digital skills lacking in 38% of skill-shortage vacancies.
TechFirst package (Industrial Strategy, GBP187m) explicitly funds AI, cyber security and computer science skills as an IS-8 cross-sector priority.
Basic numerical skills lacking in 26% of skill-shortage vacancies in 2024; complex numerical/statistical skills lacking in 25%.
Life Sciences is 1 of Skills England's 10 priority sectors, but its lab-facing occupations are not among those named in 4 or more sectors.
Industrial Strategy engineering package (over GBP100m) names engineering skills as critical across Advanced Manufacturing, Clean Energy and Digital & Technologies.
Industrial Strategy construction package: over GBP600m to train up to 60,000 more skilled construction workers; ESS: adapting to new equipment lacking in 26% of SSVs.
Clean Energy Industries employment is projected to grow 77% by 2030, the fastest of Skills England's 10 priority sectors.

Creative and innovative thinking was lacking in 43% of skill-shortage vacancies in 2024, up from 40% in 2022.
